title: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)
overview: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is the principle that encourages businesses to contribute to communities and society without expecting direct financial returns. This principle is most effectively illustrated when CSR practices foster connections between businesses and the community by addressing social issues and interests. The challenge lies in striking a balance between benefiting the community and ensuring that these practices also yield advantages for the business. This course will explore CSR methods, tools, principles, and practices, along with the ethics of CSR, effective communication strategies, and the challenges associated with CSR and how to address them.
audience: This course is aimed at professionals in private companies, NGOs, local, regional, and international organizations, as well as government entities who are currently involved in CSR or wish to integrate CSR into their institutions.
methodology: The training course is designed to be interactive and participatory, utilizing films and videos, individual and team exercises, case studies, and scenarios to enhance learning outcomes.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the history, concepts, and Carroll's four-part definition of corporate social responsibility
Outline the significance of CSR in both the public and private sectors
Recognize the convergence of business ethics, CSR, and corporate governance
Illustrate the evolution and revolution of CSR
Implement the ten rules for effective CSR communication to achieve optimal outcomes
Create a competitive advantage by identifying various CSR challenges
